chapter: Fish fries, passing the hat and district living
title: Emma Davis, long cuffs, Chicago flats and John B. Stetson hats
summary: Dawson recalls Emma Davis bringing his supper while he played at Hunts and Nagel's, and describes the clothes of the time: cuffs, Chicago flats, Edwin Clapp shoes and Stetsons.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Oh, boy, that woman used to be good that time. You had, if you had a woman up there hustling, she was good. Uh-huh. She cared for you. She's gonna, she's gonna hustle and give you anything you want. Uh-huh. Yeah. I had a woman called Emma Davis that I could, when I was at Hunts, uh, at Hunts and Nagel, so, that woman was crazy about me. And she'd give me anything. They'd send my sup up there when I be playing. And I'd stop playing music like the band playing. Now I'd have to put the chair there and put my sup, eat, eat, take my time and eat, you know. I'd stand by playing until I'd finish eating, put a napkin up and running, cause people would get my shirt there. And every time, you know, you see, you see those long sleeve shirts?
Yeah.
They was popular at that time, it had cuffs.
Uh-huh.
They had cuffs, and at that time they had, you'd wear cufflinks there. And there you'd get a nice stuff
and leave that cuff stick out a little above your coat, the sleeve of your coat. Always dressed up there.
What kind of shoes did you wear?
They had Chicago flats that time.
Huh?

Yeah, they didn't have no heel on them. They're flat, flat, flat, flat, uh, so. I never saw that. Anybody can tell you about it. You could get them shoes made. There was a little narrow heel, very narrow heel on the sole. They called them Chicago flats. You go to the store and they take your measure, make your pair of them, two toes.
But who made shoes then?
Yeah, I had shoe stoves there, used to make them.
You didn't wear Edmund Clapp's, did you?

Did I? Sure, indeed. That's the main shoes I used to wear, Edmund Clapp's, all them big-time shoes. I wear them old cheap shoes. I used to wear all them good shoes. You wasn't in the racket if you come around there with that gang I was a bummer with. You know, a pair of, uh, two, uh, beat-out shoes, you know, then, they came to their own shoes. You had to be, you had to be a big shop at the time.
And hats, who made good hats?
Hats. Stutson.
John B.
Pure old John B. Stutson. Uh-huh. And they had to have the name in the hat, too.
Yeah.
They can't go around like they'd buy all these old cheap hats and these doors, uh, uh, John B. Stutson.
